evidence_class: mocked: a local durable directory backend behind a granted artifact store, fixture launch registrations, a backend wrapper that loses acknowledgements and a fake clock; no object store, worker Pod or harness was used. Live G8 qualification belongs to the integration package.
interfaces: Publisher.publish(doc, materials) refuses scope_mismatch before any upload when the manifest authority is not the granted store scope, invalid_sequence unless checkpoint_sequence is a non-negative integer, and identity_conflict when a manifest is already committed under the checkpoint id with other content; it refuses superseded_generation when a pointer of a newer task generation exists, scope_mismatch when another execution already holds a pointer of this generation, and stale_sequence for a checkpoint_sequence at or below this generation's pointer; otherwise it reclaims any orphan materials an interrupted attempt left under the checkpoint id, uploads every material under the immutable artifact id checkpoint_id.role, checks the generation fence, commits the manifest through Validator.commit only after every object reads back verified, checks the fence again, writes the pointer keyed by task generation and checkpoint_sequence, and checks the fence once more, reporting superseded_generation if a newer generation wrote meanwhile

A replay of a promoted checkpoint with identical content re-verifies it and returns promoted with reason replayed, adding nothing; a replay whose objects no longer verify is refused with the verification reason

Publisher.latest() reads only the newest generation that holds a pointer and returns its highest sequence whose recorded manifest matches the pointer and verifies authoritative; it never falls back to an older generation, and a stale attempt cannot verify a newer generation's manifest

Publisher.sequence() gives this generation's highest pointer sequence; Publisher.reclaim(checkpoint_id) removes the manifest and material records of the named checkpoint when no pointer names it, never a newer generation's record, and removes each object no other record names once; publish calls it for its own id before a first upload, and no sweep reclaims other unpointed checkpoints

worker.supervisor.Schedule.tick() captures and publishes when due, then stretches the next interval so capture time stays within Budget.overhead of it; a lost acknowledgement counts interrupted and the same captured checkpoint is republished under its identity on the next tick; superseded_generation stops periodic promotion

Schedule.drain() publishes off schedule under its own Budget.drain deadline and Budget.drain_attempts, refusing drain_budget_exceeded when capture overruns the deadline; Schedule.metrics() adds checkpoint_age_seconds

redaction.scrub(data) runs the strict secret scan over a native conversation file: JSON object, array and string lines value by value (a value whose key makes the redacted value match again is hidden whole), every other run of lines as one text; it returns the redacted bytes and the number of markers placed, and raises secret_unredactable when a value or text opens more private keys than it closes

native.capture scrubs every collected file before NativeCapture is built, so the snapshot path and the native checkpoint keep only redacted bytes; NativeCapture.fields() adds secret_redactions when it is above zero; the archive bound applies to the redacted files

hooks.secrets private_key matches a header with any algorithm word or none, so a bare header now also blocks a write in standard mode; the strict-only nested_secret pattern matches a keyword key whose value is an object holding a value, password, passwd, token or secret field with a literal of eight or more characters, one level deep in raw text; standard mode is unchanged for that shape

Publisher.publish scrubs native_session material again before any upload and records secret_redactions on the manifest as the capture count plus its own; it refuses native_format_changed, native_too_large or secret_unredactable before any upload

rollback: Stop calling Schedule.tick and Schedule.drain to stop periodic promotion; pointers and manifests already written stay, so Publisher.latest keeps returning the last complete checkpoint. Lowering the checkpoint write_minor below 2 makes Validator.commit refuse promotion_disabled, which the publisher reports without writing a pointer. Rehearsed in case C: with write_minor 1 a publish is refused promotion_disabled and latest stays on the last complete checkpoint; restoring write_minor promotes the same checkpoint.
limitations: No production caller yet: the Pod supervisor drain path and the recovery Checkpoints listing do not call the publisher; SV2-CKP-05 owns restore decisions
git_capture.checkpoint and the native checkpoint commit manifests directly and are not fenced by generation; only Publisher.publish promotes

The pointer write is a plain backend write after the fence checks, not a conditional create; a pointer an older generation writes in the last window is reported superseded_generation and never read by latest
The drain budget bounds the capture before publish; a publish already started is not interrupted, and a lost acknowledgement retries at the next interval
The rollback was rehearsed on the local backend only, not against a deployed worker

The fence reads pointers, not grants: a newer generation that holds its grant but has written no pointer yet does not fence an older attempt, and latest can still return the older generation's checkpoint until it writes
A refused publish after its uploads leaves orphan materials until the next publish of the same checkpoint id reclaims them; there is no background sweep
Each publish lists every pointer up to four times; pointers grow by one per promoted checkpoint with no compaction
Two record keys that are themselves secrets and redact to the same marker collapse to one field; the count stays exact and no value is kept
